subject: Onboard request: pavo-13b variant + temporary version pin for latency investigation

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onboard request: pavo-13b variant + temporary version pin for latency investigation

Dylan —

Quick ask from Product: Pavo (partner) sent over a 13B variant (internal name: pavo-13b-v1) for early integration with our Dedicated EU pool. They ran a short canary and reported intermittent 400–600ms token latency spikes compared to their baseline. Before we proceed with broader routing we need a short, controlled onboarding so we can: 

- run a compatibility check (tokenizer, kv cache, attention kernel compatibility)
- confirm memory & batching characteristics on our kernels (A100/rtx pools)
- temporarily pin traffic to a safe variant while we run telemetry to reproduce the anomaly

Can you own the engineering coordination? Goal: 72-hour pin on a small dedicated pool + collection of the detailed telemetry described below. Pavo needs the schedule this week.

Attachments: [Attachment: pavo_spec_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Model Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboard request: pavo-13b variant + temporary version pin for latency investigation

Acknowledged. I'll take point on the compatibility and rollout plan. Summary of immediate next steps I need from Eng and Security: 

1) Compatibility checklist (tokenizer version, tokenizer vocabulary differences, expected max sequence, kv cache growth pattern).
2) Kernel/quantization compatibility (Marcus, can you confirm if pavo-13b uses any custom ops or unsupported attention layouts?).
3) Canary configuration: allocate a 4-GPU dedicated EU pool, route 1% traffic for initial stability window, then ramp to 10% if stable.
4) Telemetry requirements: per-token latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), gc pauses, kernel time breakdown, and KV cache hit/miss ratio. Put outputs in a shared folder and link the HubSpot deal (Laura linked).
5) Temporary pin: propose a 72-hour pin to pavo-13b-qcandidate (a read-only pinned alias) during the investigation; after 72 hours we assess whether to unpin or route to fallback.

Priyom — can you own the instrumentation and run the first compatibility checklist today? Marcus — can you scope the kernel compatibility run and estimate time? Ava — note Laura's and Pavo's ask to keep this in EU; flag anything we need for KMS or SOC2 evidence.

Quote from original: 
> Pavo reported intermittent 400–600ms token latency spikes compared to their baseline.

If anyone can't meet the timeline, call it out and we'll adjust the schedule.

—Dylan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboard request: pavo-13b variant + temporary version pin for latency investigation

Thanks — initial read on the artifact (quick local smoke): tokenizer uses sentencepiece v1.0 with some extra control tokens, but no unusual vocab size. Two notes from infra: 

- The model includes a custom fused attention op that falls back to our generic kernel on current runtime; fallback shows increased kernel launch overhead at short sequence lengths — plausible source of token spikes.
- There are two weight format variants in the manifest (fp16 and q4_0). The q4_0 path reduces memory and tends to have more stable kernel scheduling on our runtime.

Proposed technical plan: 
A) Run a focused compat suite (tokenization round-trip, KV persistence, attention microbench) on a 4xA100 EU pool. I estimate 6–8 hours to complete the suite end-to-end.
B) For the temporary pin, I recommend pinning to pavo-13b-q4_0 (the quantized build) as the safe variant. It matches Pavo's functionally but avoids the fallback path in our RT kernels.
C) Canary wiring: run 1% traffic for 4 hours; if p99 token latency stays within +15% of baseline and no kernel-level OOMs, ramp to 10% for 24h; collect traces and group by sequence length.

Attaching a short runbook and the minimal tests I'll run.
Attachments: [Attachment: compat-check-runbook.md (Markdown, 8KB)]

I'll start the compat suite at 16:00 PT and post results to the shared folder and the HubSpot deal.

—Marcus

Couple of compliance items before we wire traffic to EU pools: 

1) Data residency: Pavo has asked for EU-only serving and logs. Confirm whether weights are EU-hosted and whether our temporary pin will route any telemetry outside the EU.
2) KMS: If Pavo requires customer-managed keys for weights access, we need the key ARN and a short IAM policy.
3) Evidence: they asked for SOC2 and encryption-in-transit docs. We can provide a link to our compliance pack but need to know whether they require any additional attestation.

Laura / Pavo — please confirm the above. If Pavo will provide EU weights (S3 EU-only) and they accept our SOC2 link, we can proceed.

Quoted:

Ava
